about.desc: ArcBlog is a Blocklet blog: DID Wallet identity is the author credential, posts are Markdown-first, and images live in the Arc file space.
about.lifecycle-desc: Posts follow a draft → published → archived lifecycle with optimistic concurrency and a full audit trail. Soft deletes keep records recoverable.
about.title: About ArcBlog
agents.admin-only: Sign in as an administrator to see this list.
agents.agent-closed: Default-closed (spec §130): settle_payment, change_wallet, change_role never run from the agent surface.
agents.agent-grants-empty: How to grant one: node scripts/arcblog-agent.mjs authorize --agent <did> --capability agent.write --ttl 30
agents.desc: What the agent surface can do to this node: the enforced policy, the declared tool catalogue, the grant records and the operator CLI that issues them.
agents.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to view agent grants and policy.
agents.grant-desc: Grants are addressed by sha256(agentDid).slice(0,16), and the AUP DSL has no hash primitive, so this page cannot sign or revoke one. Use the operator CLI: it requires an explicit expiry and keeps high-risk capabilities behind a second confirmation.
agents.grant-forbidden: agent.admin is not grantable and cannot be granted: settle_payment, change_wallet and change_role never run from the agent surface (spec §130).
agents.grants-desc: Records under config/agent-grants/ (admin-only). A write tool only runs while its grant is unexpired.
agents.mutations: This console reports state only. Value-bearing mutations (settlement, wallets, roles, payments) stay deliberate CLI actions with a DID session.
agents.policy-desc: Enforced by scripts/arcblog-agent.mjs and audited by node scripts/arcblog-agent.mjs check. Read-only: this page has no switches.
agents.runtime-note: Spec §129: /mcp, /api/afs/rpc and llms.txt are provided by the ARC Runtime; ArcBlog only declares and audits them, so this page does not assert their runtime availability.
agents.studio-registry: no cross-node Studio registry in this platform version (spec §71 is a POST-MVP transport)
agents.title: Agent capabilities & tools
agents.tools-closed-note: Closed tools never run from the agent surface: orders / settlements / sales name buyers (admin-only, privacy); settle_payment, change_wallet and change_role are default-closed.
agents.tools-desc: Every tool the agent surface declares, with the capability it needs and whether it can run today. Read tools are always on; write tools need a time-boxed grant; closed tools never run.
agents.tools-legend: Status: available = runs today; unavailable = declared but the platform cannot serve it (reason inline).
agents.tools-source: Source: node scripts/arcblog-agent.mjs tools — 19 tools (read 9 / write 4 / closed 6). Re-run the CLI to re-verify.
agents.tools-write: Write tools (4) — require a time-boxed grant
appearance.desc: Theme, tone and palette for this site. Admins set the defaults; signed-in users can personalize their own theme.
appearance.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to set this site's palette and tone. Signed-in users can also personalize their own theme.
appearance.title: Appearance
categories.add-note: A page write stores sort=0; adjust it afterwards with the CLI in the advanced section below. The CLI accepts only lowercase letters, digits and hyphens (slugify).
categories.adv-desc: These commands do the same work as the buttons above, plus what this page does not offer (sort, seed, usage counts). Kept for operators who prefer the shell.
categories.cat-remove-msg: A bare delete (no migration) stays a CLI-only action: it is only safe when nothing references the category, and this page cannot prove that. Use the buttons above — they always migrate first.
categories.cat-slug-hint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, e.g. technology.
categories.cmd-merge: Merge this category into another (migrates every referencing post)
categories.cmd-remove-migrate: Migrate the references, then remove it (never leaves a dangling category)
categories.desc: Taxonomy used by the publish validator and the public feed. Every governance action is a button: it queues an intent, and this node's worker does the rewrite. No terminal needed.
categories.enqueue-failed: Could not queue the intent — nothing was written. Sign in as the blocklet owner and try again.
categories.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to manage the site.
categories.gov-desc: Merge a category into another, or delete it while migrating its posts. In the row you want to change, type the target slug into that row's target field, then press its button: the button only queues the action — this node's worker performs the rewrite, so the browser never touches your posts.
categories.list-desc: One row per record under /instance/app/arcblog/categories/ (live-subscribed), showing the stored sort value. Reference counts are deliberately NOT displayed: a page-side count could only come from the query index, which goes stale after an edit (arc-contracts §15), so the advanced section gives you the usage command instead — it scans the records directly.
categories.list-empty-hint: An empty list means no category record exists yet — the publish validator then falls back to the built-in technology / design / life.
categories.merge-confirm-msg: Every post or draft referencing this category is rewritten to the target category, then the source record is removed, by this node's worker. Nothing is queued until you press OK.
categories.queue-clear-msg: Removes the record from the queue. Posts it already rewrote are unaffected.
categories.queue-desc: The console cannot rewrite posts itself, so a button only queues an intent. The worker applies it with the same code path as the CLI merge — and writes the outcome (applied / rejected / noop + reason) back onto this record.
categories.queue-legend: pending = waiting for the worker · applied = posts rewritten, source record removed · noop = nothing to do (already done) · rejected = refused, no data changed
categories.queue-standing-note: Every queued intent record appears in the list above, newest first: a row is written the moment a button is clicked, so an empty list simply means nothing has been queued on this node yet.
categories.queued: Intent queued — the local worker applies it.
categories.remove-confirm-msg: Every post or draft referencing this category is migrated to the target category, then the category record itself is deleted — by this node's worker, so the category is never left dangling (spec §15.4).
categories.sort-desc: `sort` is a real record field and the CLI lists by (sort, slug): technology 10 / design 20 / life 30. This page never edits it — change it with the CLI command in the advanced section. Ordering is CLI-only: this page exposes no other reordering interface.
categories.status-note: The status text is read verbatim from the record. This platform cannot pick a localized label per record (a dynamic $t() key renders literally), so the machine value is shown — docs/arc-contracts.md §28.8.
categories.target-hint: Every row has its own target field: type the slug of an existing category there (the list below shows every slug). An unknown or empty target is refused by the worker with a reason — nothing is changed.
categories.title: Categories
categories.worker-note: Buttons only queue the action. The node's worker (node scripts/arcblog-category.mjs watch) performs it — the browser never rewrites a post. This platform cannot run server-side code from a button click.
compose-edit.desc: Edit this draft, then save it back to the private drafts or publish it to the site.
compose-edit.not-found: Draft not found. Open the studio to pick an existing draft.
compose-edit.title: Edit post
compose.desc: Write a story, then save it as a private draft or publish it to the site.
compose.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to unlock the editor. Drafts stay in the private drafts directory until published.

dashboard.content-guide: Write and publish from Write; the newest five stories appear here.
dashboard.drafts-desc: The three most recently updated records in the private drafts area.
dashboard.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to see the drafts waiting for you and what is already live.
dashboard.pagesize-note: Pagination note (BUG-063): the per-page selector (“Show”) is stored by THIS browser as localStorage['aup-list-pagesize:<list id>'] and overrides the page default. Choosing a value ≥ the total makes the platform drop the whole paginator — including the selector itself — so no in-page control can bring it back. Recovery: clear this site's data, or delete that localStorage key, then reload.
dashboard.purpose: What needs you now: the drafts still to finish, and what is already live.
dashboard.title: Dashboard
diagnostics.adv-desc: Level-3 detail, folded here: storage & index, the log surface, data export / backup, the permission surface, the background intent queue and first-line troubleshooting. Every command is copy-and-run; nothing on this page executes. How to read them: run the storage audit bare — it answers through its exit code (0 = every layout is files and the index is fresh) and its JSON report grows past 64KB, so a piped fragment is not a report (arc-contracts §4.1a). arc space sync converges --to toward --from and --mirror DELETES destination-only files, so preview with --dry-run. The AFS records are the source of truth and dist/ is rebuildable, so keep an OFFLINE copy of node.key (content-signing key) and .env.local (chain configuration) outside this repo — they are not AFS records; losing them loses the node identity, and they must never be committed or written into AFS. DID Space: /user is a caller-scoped projection, not a directory — arc space list --scope user and arc space path --scope user address it (substitute the app DID), and the reading-list CLI addresses records by reader DID; this daemon has AFS_DID_SPACE_SCOPE_SECRET UNSET, so scope directories are plaintext (de-identification OFF) — a daemon environment variable ArcBlog can only register as a production prerequisite, never set. Permissions: this platform gives the app exactly two roles, guest and admin (blocklet.yaml replicated.readRole / minRole) — there is no finer grant to look for. Background work: a console chain button only writes an intent record; the node's own worker signs it on the chain (the signing key never reaches the browser) — that is the worker command above. No heartbeat record exists anywhere in this codebase, so an empty queue is a normal state, not an error, and there is no last-seen time to show.
diagnostics.cmd-backup: Preview a mirror export (writes nothing); drop --dry-run to run it
diagnostics.cmd-check: Audit storage and index, read-only (run it bare and read the exit code; --folder <space-dir> audits one claimed folder)
diagnostics.cmd-logs: The only log surface: the daemon log (add --json, or -i <instance>)
diagnostics.cmd-perm: Re-run the guest permission matrix alone
diagnostics.cmd-record: Run the self-check and record it — the source of the summary above; --help lists the checks and the record shape
diagnostics.cmd-repair: Rebuild one folder's ledger from disk
diagnostics.cmd-worker: Keep draining pending chain intents (long-running); run drains once
diagnostics.desc: Is this node healthy right now? The verdict of the last recorded self-check, when it ran, and every check one row at a time. This page executes nothing: it only visualises the recorded result and offers commands you copy and run yourself. Level-3 detail — commands, storage, logs, backup, permissions, background work, troubleshooting — is folded into the Advanced tab.
diagnostics.faq: A save looked accepted but the record is unchanged: the toast is not evidence — read the record back with arc afs exec /blocklets/arcblog/.actions/read --args '{"path":"<afs path>"}' --json (arc-contracts §29.4). A write was refused: conditional, not absolute — it depends on the record's origin, the write mode and the daemon process (§29.2); probe before deleting, because delete + recreate loses createdAt. A record disappeared from a filtered list: filter / serverFilters push a query to the index and an edit leaves its index entry stale (§15) — re-check through arc afs exec /blocklets/arcblog/.actions/list --args '{"path":"<dir>"}' --json. ?page=<id> silently lands on the public home: that id is not a registered page — the authoritative page set is the sidebar model, guarded in the fast tier (npm test). A read is denied for a signed-in session: the record's directory prefix decides (blocklet.yaml replicated.readRole / minRole, §13); there is no third role to grant. Storage keeps growing: audit read-only first, then rebuild one folder's ledger (both commands above); dev-instance test residue is swept by arcblog-clean.mjs, dry-run by default. A publish never reached the public site: record a self-check (command above) and read the space-layout / resources rows; Node registry state lives on ?page=registry.
diagnostics.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to see this instance's self-check results.
diagnostics.list-desc: One record per check, live-subscribed; the row count is whatever the last run recorded — this page hard-codes no number. severity and ok are shown as text, so a state never depends on colour alone.
diagnostics.sum-empty: No self-check snapshot yet — 尚未运行: nothing has been recorded here, so this card shows no verdict and no invented time. Empty is not the same as “all checks passed”. Run the record command on the Advanced tab first.
diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
factory.actions-desc: One click queues the intent; the node's chain worker signs it (the key never reaches the browser) and the queue below updates live.
factory.advanced-note: Addresses and transaction hashes read from node/factories.json; the public key is bound into the on-chain NFT template, and no key material is mirrored here. Whether a value is chain truth is decided PER NODE, never from the file header — see the attribution card.
factory.chain-empty: No factory yet. Create one: node scripts/arcblog-factory.mjs create --role studio --adapter ocap
factory.confirm-acquire-msg: The factory mints one Studio node NFT to this node's owner wallet, on chain, immediately.
factory.confirm-claim-msg: The NFT returns to the owner wallet and the stake closes.
factory.confirm-revoke-msg: Assets leave the stake and a waiting period starts before the final claim (spec §8.4).
factory.confirm-stake-msg: The NFT locks into the factory stake and the role becomes staked (spec §8.3).
factory.desc: The on-chain identity of this node: the SVG card it renders, the factories that mint it, and one-click buy / stake / revoke / claim.
factory.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to view the node NFT and operate it.
factory.intent-queued: Intent queued — watch the queue below.
factory.node-empty: No node NFT yet — press Buy / mint below.
factory.projection: Read from the public projection node/factories.json; the authoritative records stay in config/ (admin-only). No key material is mirrored.
factory.queue-admin: The queue lives in config/ (admin-only): only the blocklet owner can queue or watch chain operations.
factory.queue-clear-msg: Removes the record from the queue. The chain transaction is unaffected.
factory.queue-standing-note: Every queued chain intent appears in the list above, oldest first: a row is written the moment a button is clicked, so an empty list simply means nothing has been queued on this node yet.
factory.render-timing: First-load note: on this platform the projection is bound AFTER the first render, so on a cold visit every field below can read the empty placeholder — that means "not bound yet / unavailable", never "the record is empty". Expand the advanced details or reload once to bind it (measured 2026-09-28: no channel recovers on its own).
factory.status-note: The dot and the status text are read from the record. This platform cannot pick a localized label per record (a dynamic $t() key renders literally), so the machine value is shown verbatim — docs/arc-contracts.md §28.8.
factory.title: Node NFT
factory.truth-note: Each node records the adapter that produced its facts, in THREE states — mock (simulation, never chain truth) · ocap (real chain, verifiable) · unknown (nothing was ever recorded; then `simulated` is null and `simulationUnknown` is true, i.e. no false 'not simulated' claim — D37b). The header adapter describes config/nft-factories.json only (adapterScope), so it must never be used to decide whether a node is chain truth (BUG-043/046 · arc-contracts §32(9)).
factory.truth-title: Is it really on chain? (per node)
feeds.desc: Subscription and index surfaces generated from published content.
feeds.feeds-agent: Agent access (llms.txt / MCP) is declared by the runtime.
feeds.feeds-desc: These surfaces are built by the CLI, not by the runtime: run node scripts/arcblog-rss.mjs to generate the RSS artifact — until it has run, /p/rss.xml does not exist.
feeds.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to view the distribution surfaces.

general.basics-desc: Site-level values. They live in this blocklet's own config collection and are read by the RSS generator.
general.basics-error: Not saved — the write was refused and nothing changed. Check that a value is chosen (or filled in) and that the runtime allows the write; the console shows the platform error.
general.basics-guard: Each field offers only its own record’s allowed values, so this page cannot submit an out-of-options value, and a field must be chosen (or filled) explicitly before Save. The current values are shown under “Stored records” — that list is the source of truth. Two platform notes: on a brand-new tab the prefill can stay empty until the page is reloaded or reached by an in-page menu click (arc-contracts §21.11), and the readers fall back to the documented default if a record was written out-of-band — see `node scripts/arcblog-settings.mjs general show`.
general.desc: Instance-level General settings: site name, language, timezone and the three Instance switches. One home for every "where is that switch?" question.
general.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to manage this instance's General settings.
general.init-confirm-msg: Creates any missing record with its documented default. Existing records are left untouched (the platform refuses to overwrite an existing path in create mode).
general.init-desc: Create only the records that are missing, with their documented default; an existing record is never overwritten (create mode refuses an existing path). These are ordinary records: the CLI and this page can both update them afterwards — arc-contracts §29.2 (corrected in Round 10) says a browser write to an existing record is not refused in general; it depends on the origin of the record, the write mode and the daemon process. If a Save ever fails, probe before deleting anything: delete + recreate loses createdAt.
general.language-hint: Value of the RSS <language> element of the generated feed.
general.records-desc: What is actually stored under /instance/app/arcblog/config/general/. This list is the source of truth: if an edit above is refused, the value here does not change.
general.roles-cmd-init: Change the address / network from the CLI (the only path)
general.roles-config-desc: Collection address, network, assetType and the declared lifecycle are record values (config/roles.json, spec §9, admin-only). This page only displays them; the record is the authority and the CLI below is the only way to change it.
general.roles-desc: Spec §15.9. This card shows the ENGINE's own role state: the five lifecycle words and every derived value come from scripts/lib/roles.mjs and its CLI, never from a second vocabulary typed into a page. The externalized config is read-only here (spec §9), and changing an address or a network is a CLI/operator step only.
general.roles-factory-desc: These four actions already live on the Node NFT page and are NOT duplicated here: each one queues an intent record there and the node's chain worker signs it. This card only links there, so the purchase-to-stake guide stays inside the console (spec §15.9).
general.roles-honesty: Honesty note: a leftover assetId in the record (for example a test value) does NOT mean an asset is owned — assetOwned is derived from the lifecycle state. And this re-derivation is NOT a chain verification: chainVerification stays false and no value on this card is chain truth (spec §114/§115).
general.roles-no-input: There is no address and no network input on this page, on purpose — spec §1273 forbids typing an address into the UI. A value shown as unbound means "not bound yet / unavailable", never "the record is empty".
general.roles-source-note: Authoritative source for every value: node scripts/arcblog-roles.mjs status (RoleStatus) and capabilities. This card renders a projection; when the two disagree, the CLI wins.
general.roles-states: Lifecycle (source: STAKE_STATES in scripts/lib/roles.mjs): none → acquired → staked → revoking → claimable. The page repeats these five words verbatim so that a drift is visible, and revoking derives to claimable at read time once claimableAt has passed — the record itself is not rewritten.
general.roles-states-note: Every state here is operator-declared: setting staked does NOT activate a role. Until a verifier exists every chain role stays active=false and its capabilities stay withheld (fail closed, spec §114/§115). This card never asserts that a role is active.
general.roles-status-desc: Derived by the CLI (never typed here) from config/roles.json + node/factories.json + node/profile.json and landed under node/role-status/. The reason string is rendered verbatim in English: this console cannot translate a runtime value, and a paraphrase would hide the real cause.
general.roles-verify-confirm-msg: Writes one intent record only; the snapshot changes when the worker runs. Nothing is verified on chain.
general.roles-verify-desc: The button queues ONE intent record under config/role-verify-intents/<id>.json (admin-only, the same config collection as the policy queue — zero permission change). It runs nothing itself and never touches config/roles.json. The node's worker consumes it:
general.roles-verify-error: Not queued — the write was refused and nothing changed.
general.roles-verify-kind: What the worker does: a READ-ONLY re-derivation of every RoleStatus from the existing records; it writes node/role-status/<role>.json + node/role-verification.json and reports whether config/roles.json and the public node/factories.json projection agree. It never flips chainVerification and signs nothing.
general.roles-verify-queue: writes: /instance/app/arcblog/config/role-verify-intents/<timestamp>.json with status pending — read it back; a toast is not evidence.
general.roles-verify-title: Re-verify — the real path (no fake button)
general.scope-desc: These are Instance-level values: they are stored at /instance/app/arcblog/config/{general,switches}/<field>.json and apply to the whole node. The impact of every switch is written next to it below.
general.site-name-hint: Channel title of the generated RSS feed. It does not rename the blocklet or the console brand.
general.sw-agent-consumer: Consumed by scripts/arcblog-agent.mjs: when off, `run` refuses every tool and `check` reports the switch as disabled (fail closed). Takes effect on the next CLI run.
general.sw-agent-impact: Impact: every Agent Access tool call on this node. It does not affect the read-only public web surface.
general.sw-comments-consumer: No consumer yet — ArcBlog has no comment feature at all, so this switch is recorded only. It is not a fake control: the page says so, and the record is readable by the CLI.
general.sw-comments-impact: Impact: none today. Planned to gate a comment surface if one is built (spec §15.9).
general.sw-rss-consumer: Consumed by scripts/arcblog-rss.mjs: when off, the generated feed keeps its channel but carries no <item>. Takes effect on the next feed generation.
general.sw-rss-impact: Impact: the public RSS feed (and therefore every subscriber). It does not remove published posts.
general.switches-desc: Instance-level master switches. Every switch states its impact and whether anything actually consumes it.
general.timezone-hint: IANA timezone used for the <pubDate>/<lastBuildDate> UTC offset of the generated feed.
general.title: Settings

heroes.desc: Home carousel records: title, image URL, target link and sort order.
heroes.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to manage the site.
heroes.hero-admin-desc: Heroes render as the homepage carousel. Each record needs a title, an image URL, and a target link; sort orders the slides ascending.
heroes.hero-delete-msg: This removes the hero record permanently.
heroes.hero-dropzone-desc: Upload an image here, then paste the resulting URL into the form above.
heroes.hero-id-hint: Lowercase letters, numbers and dashes; same ID overwrites.
heroes.hero-quickadd-hint: Click a post row to stage it below, then confirm. Title, summary, cover and /posts/<slug> link are copied automatically.

media.adv-cmds: Media commands — copy this line, then pick one verb and fill in the id / AFS path
media.cmd-refs: Show where one asset is used (read-only information)
media.desc: Upload an asset, read this node's upload index, and reach the CLI commands that compute references and clean up (Advanced tab).
media.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to view the media index.
media.index-note: Each row is one record of this upload index: title, MIME type, byte size, indexed time, plus two copy buttons — the asset's AFS path and the refs command for that id. The record carries no public URL, so none is shown, and the index itself is maintained by the CLI, never by this page.
media.limits-join: Platform limits, stated instead of hidden: a page cannot join collections, so reference data (refs, and the unreferenced list) is computed only by the CLI; the media collection is admin-only, because a record exposes its upload path; the spec's list/grid switch is not implemented (afs-list layout=grid is locked to 6 auto-fill columns and a columns prop is ignored at runtime — docs/arc-contracts.md §25); and no record stores a public URL.
media.media-standing-note: The list above renders every record of this upload index. An empty list only means no asset has been indexed on this node yet — index one with the CLI command in the Advanced tab. This platform cannot probe a list's length, and emptyText does not evaluate translations (docs/arc-contracts.md §19/§20), so this is a standing note, never a claim about the rows above.
media.orphans-order: Always run refs --id <id> first: it shows where the asset is used before you clean anything up.
media.orphans-record-only: remove deletes the index record only — it never deletes the binary file.
media.orphans-refuse: remove is refused while the asset is still referenced (exit 1, code CONFLICT): resolve the references first, or pass --force to override.
media.refs-note: refs prints the count plus each referring record (kind + slug + path) from posts / drafts / pages / page-drafts / heroes.
media.title: Media
media.upload-desc: Pick or drop a file. afs-dropzone is the platform's only upload primitive and is declared without props on purpose: this platform exposes no prop metadata for it (arc dsl schema), so no prop is invented.
media.upload-note: Measured 2026-09-27 on this instance: dropping a file fails with "Upload failed: targetDir must be a non-empty string" — the prop-less form is this repo's existing convention, so no prop is invented here. Even a successful upload would not create an index record: the binary lands in your own DID space, so the index stays CLI-maintained — the command is in the Advanced tab.
operations.desc: Live state of this node: health, discovery, Hubs, economy, media and agent grants.
operations.discovery-empty: How to publish it: node scripts/arcblog-network.mjs discovery publish
operations.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to view node health and discovery.
operations.hubs-empty: How to add one: node scripts/arcblog-network.mjs hub register --hub-did <did>
operations.render-timing: First-load note: on this platform the health / discovery projections are bound AFTER the first render, so a cold visit can show the empty placeholder for every field below — read that as "not bound yet / unavailable", never as "the record is empty". Reload once to bind it (measured 2026-09-28).
operations.title: Operations
page-view.title: Page
pages.act-delete-msg: Pages have no soft delete — this removes the record.
pages.act-offline-msg: Queues ONE "Take offline" intent under config/page-intents/ — this page writes nothing to your records. This node's worker performs the move (it reads the page, merges it into page-drafts/, then removes the public copy): `arcblog-pages.mjs apply` once, or `watch` to keep it running. Read the intent record back — a toast is not evidence.
pages.act-publish-msg: Queues ONE "Bring online" intent under config/page-intents/ — this page writes nothing to your records. This node's worker writes the public copy and removes the offline copy; an older public copy (written by the old CLI or by root authority) is replaced too, because the worker writes with this node's own authority — the very write the platform refuses when a page asks for it.
pages.created-ok: Page created offline. Bring it online when ready.
pages.desc: Standalone pages such as About. Two states only — online and offline; no post lifecycle, no RSS, no Hub indexing.
pages.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to manage standalone pages.
pages.list-empty: No pages yet. Create your first page above.
pages.offline-hint: Offline pages are admin-only. 「Bring online」 only queues an intent under config/page-intents/; the local worker performs the move (arcblog-pages.mjs queue prints those rows read-only, apply runs them once, watch keeps running). The list below the two page lists is that queue, read straight from AFS: action · status · message.
pages.offline-ok: Intent queued — read config/page-intents to confirm; the local worker takes the page offline.
pages.online-hint: Online pages are public at /pages/<slug>; they stay out of RSS and the Hub index. 「Take offline」 only queues an intent under config/page-intents/ — the local worker completes the move. 「Remove public copy」 is a different, immediate action: it hard-deletes the public record (pages have no soft delete).
pages.published-ok: Intent queued — read config/page-intents to confirm; the local worker brings the page online.
pages.title: Pages
posts.admin-archive-msg: Archive this post? Writes a copy into the private drafts directory with status archived. The public post stays online until you remove it from public.
posts.admin-delete-msg: Soft-delete this record? The record stays in the private drafts directory with status deleted and can be republished later.
posts.admin-publish-msg: Publish a copy of this draft? This page COPIES the draft into the public posts/ directory and keeps the source draft here (copy semantics). The CLI publish command is different: it moves the record and deletes the source draft.
posts.admin-unpublish-msg: Remove this post from public? Deletes the record from the public posts directory. Archive first if you want to keep a private copy.
posts.cli-note: Move semantics and bulk work stay in the CLI: node scripts/arcblog-lifecycle.mjs archive moves posts/ → drafts/, publish and republish move drafts/ → posts/, soft-delete marks a private record deleted. The console copies instead of moving, and drafts/ is one private directory (draft + archived + deleted) — the Archived tab is that same directory narrowed by each record's own archivedAt stamp.
posts.desc: Your stories by state: published, drafts, archived. One primary action (write) and every lifecycle action kept.
posts.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to manage drafts, published stories and uploaded media.
posts.pagesize-note: Pagination note (BUG-063): the per-page selector (“Show”) is stored by THIS browser as localStorage['aup-list-pagesize:<list id>'] and overrides the page default. Choosing a value ≥ the total makes the platform drop the whole paginator — including the selector itself — so no in-page control can bring it back. Recovery: clear this site's data, or delete that localStorage key, then reload.
posts.status-note: Per-record status is shown as the raw machine value: the platform cannot pick a localized label per record (a dynamic $t() key renders literally, docs/arc-contracts.md §28.8). Record counts are rendered by each tab's own list footer (“Total: N records”) — this page invents no number. An empty tab means that state holds no record yet; write one with the button above.

saved.desc: A private reading list. Every record lives in the signed-in reader's own user scope (/user/arcblog/bookmarks/<slug>.json), which the platform only materialises for that caller — no other visitor and no other signed-in DID resolves the same list.

saved.gov-desc: This page lists and adds; it deliberately does not delete. Measured (REQ-028): an AUP page validates ALL of its inputs on ANY action submit, so one empty required field blocks every other action on the page — a page-side delete would be hostage to the add form below. Removal is therefore the CLI's job, exactly as on the other console pages.
saved.list-desc: One row per record under /user/arcblog/bookmarks/ in this session's own user scope. The path is caller-scoped, not a shared directory: the same URL resolves to a different list for a different DID, and a signed-out visitor has no /user view at all.
saved.list-empty: Nothing saved yet. An empty list means no record exists in this reader's user scope — the form below writes the first one.
saved.slug-hint: Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, exactly as it appears in /posts/<slug>. The CLI enforces the same rule.
saved.title: Reading list
saved.where-note: Storage: /user/arcblog/bookmarks/<slug>.json (this caller's DID Space user scope, AFS path /blocklets/arcblog/users/<your-did>/arcblog/bookmarks/). ArcBlog declares no blocklet.yaml permission for it: the user scope is authorized by the session, not by a replicated collection — measured (arc-contracts.md).

tags.clear-msg: Removes the record from the queue. Posts it already rewrote are unaffected.
tags.confirm-msg: Every post referencing the source tag is rewritten in place (version + content hash), on both the published and the draft side. The console queues it; the node's worker applies it.
tags.desc: Tags are free-form words on posts — there is no tag registry. Rename or merge to converge spelling variants; the counts below come from the same scan the CLI prints.
tags.empty-body: A tag appears here as soon as a post carries one: add tags while writing, then press Refresh projection — the worker rebuilds this list from the posts. There is no tag registry.
tags.enqueue-failed: Could not queue the intent — nothing was written. Sign in as the blocklet owner and try again.
tags.f-from-hint: Pick an existing tag from the list on the right.
tags.f-hint: Stored form is lowercase with underscores; spaces, capitals and hyphens are normalized when the worker executes.
tags.f-unknown-hint: A tag that does not exist yet cannot be renamed — the worker records it as noop and writes nothing. Check the list on the right first.
tags.form-desc: A target that does not exist yet renames the tag; an existing target merges into it. Either way every referencing post is rewritten.
tags.gate-desc: Sign in with DID Wallet to manage the site.

Choosing a value ≥ the total makes the platform drop the whole paginator — including the selector itself — so no in-page control can bring it back. tags.queue-desc: The console cannot rewrite posts itself, so the form only queues an intent. The worker applies it with the same code path as the CLI merge.
tags.queue-legend: pending = waiting for the worker · applied = posts rewritten · noop = no article referenced the source tag, nothing written · rejected = refused, no post touched
tags.queued: Intent queued — the local worker applies it.
tags.refresh-hint: Counts and the timestamp come from a derived projection: Refresh queues an intent, and this node's worker rebuilds it from the posts (node scripts/arcblog-tags.mjs watch).
tags.status-note: The dot and the status text are read from the record. This platform cannot pick a localized label per record (a dynamic $t() key renders literally), so the machine value is shown verbatim — docs/arc-contracts.md §28.8.
tags.title: Tags
tags.worker-note: Queued actions are executed by the node's worker (node scripts/arcblog-tags.mjs watch), never by the browser.
general.roles-claimable-note: Waiting period: the raw claimableAt value is shown above when the record carries one; this console deliberately renders no countdown (the platform's conditional `visible` cannot gate a relative-time row on a bound value, measured 2026-09-29 — and an empty value would otherwise read as "just now").
general.roles-reason-note: How to read these rows: the label is this console's own field name and the value is the role engine's own text, rendered verbatim. Why verbatim: a `$t()` key must be a compile-time constant (arc-contracts §28.8) and `visible` only supports synchronous `$session.*` expressions (arc-contracts §28.1), so this console has no mechanism to switch a value's wording from a record value — the engine vocabulary is therefore glossed here: `granted` = the capability is granted; `withheld` = it is withheld (fail closed); `yes` / `no` = the boolean the engine derived; `(none)` = nothing is withheld (not a missing value). A granted role has nothing withheld — for `basic` the `reason` explains why the capability is implicit, not why it is withheld; a withheld capability carries its cause in the same row.
general.roles-two-stage-note: Reading the dashes: this platform renders an em dash when the bound record has no such value, or when the binding has not resolved yet — on a freshly opened tab the rows below can all read as dashes until a reload (or an in-page menu round-trip) resolves them, and the reload shows the real values. A dash never means "no roles". This note is unconditional: it does not claim that any record is missing. The authority is `node scripts/arcblog-roles.mjs status`.
pages.queue-legend: pending = queued, not run yet · applied = the worker ran it · rejected = refused, zero change · noop = already in that state
pages.queue-empty-note: Empty state: when a list has no records this platform prints its own hard-coded English empty-list text (arc-contracts §20 measures that `emptyText` is not evaluated at runtime), so this page cannot localize it. This note is standing and does not claim that any list is empty; the authority for the queue is `node scripts/arcblog-pages.mjs queue`.

dashboard.empty-guidance: Standing note, not a claim about the lists below — a brand-new node has nothing to show yet. Write a post: it stays in your private drafts until you publish it, and the newest three drafts and five published stories then appear here.
